items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: I was able to tell the same thing with Cannonball much later... I said, oh that’s Cannonball. I know that.

ctx.x: I know but it’s so funny you say that because the guys that I was fortunate enough to talk to, like Sweets Edison and that generation, they make such a thing out of that. Like “in my day you could tell a player in two measures.” Now you just said the same thing. Can you put it into words? Or maybe —

Well with Nat I would have to say it’s — well the dead giveaway would be his tone. Because he is playing cornet, and the cornet is strikingly different than the trumpet. Most trumpeters can hear the difference right off you know. The cornet has a much mellower sound, and he’s — well I was going to say he’s playing it like a trumpet. I mean he’s playing it like a trumpeter would play a trumpet, you know? And all that stuff that he’s — and then beyond that, beyond the sound of the horn, you have all these Natisms…

distorted the notes when he went up into the higher register, and then a run that he did where it was his full tone [scats] but it was just a full huge tone, and it felt like he was blowing the brass off the horn. And I said, oh that’s Cannonball. I know that. That’s Cannon. Now the saxophonist like yourself, I’m sure you’d be able to —
